land.text: Singapore: 'On 9 August 1965, the Malaysian Parliament voted 126 to 0 to pass a constitutional amendment bill, thereby separating Singapore from Malaysia'

predecessors.note: Singapore had been a self-governing state from 3 June 1959 and a state of Malaysia from 16 September 1963; Cliopatria starts its Singapore row in 1967.

correction.text: Singapore from independence on 9 August 1965; the 1967 shape unchanged, with the years extended back to 1965

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1967 and keeps Singapore inside Malaysia through 1966, but the infobox gives 'Proclamation of Singapore: 9 August 1965' and the page says Singapore 'became independent as the Republic of Singapore on 9 August 1965'. Only the years change.

691 km2 for 1967-2023 against the infobox's 744.3 km2 (no year given): ratio 0.93. The page says reclamation 'increased Singapore's land area from roughly 580 km2 in the 1960s to 770 km2 by the 2030s', so the shape (3 cells) is within the precision of the grid at every date; the gazetteer cannot draw the growth.
The same 691 km2 outline for the final year.

region.text: the island of Singapore: 'Proclamation of Singapore: 9 August 1965'

ledger.note: 1965: Singapore becomes independent as the Republic of Singapore (9 August), 'with Lee Kuan Yew and Yusof bin Ishak as the first prime minister and president respectively'.

9 August 1965: Malaysia lets Singapore go. 'The Separation Agreement was signed on 7 August 1965'; the Malaysian Parliament passed the amendment bill 126-0 on 9 August and 'Singapore became a sovereign state on 9 August'; the Yang di-Pertuan Negara, Yusof Ishak, had held office since 1959.

wars.name: Indonesia-Malaysia confrontation
wars.outcome: 'A final peace agreement was signed on 11 August 1966 with Indonesia formally recognising Malaysia'; the page records no territorial change.
wars.note: The page lists Singapore among the belligerents; Singapore was a Malaysian state until 9 August 1965. This page was opened for the malaysia dossier, not within this dossier's own two-page budget. Reviewer se-04-b (2026-10-20): 'from' set to 1965, the first year of this dossier's life; the confrontation began in 1963, while Singapore was a state of Malaysia (malaysia dossier).

certainty.note: A small island state whose frontier is its coast and the Johor Strait; the growth by reclamation (about 580 km2 in the 1960s to 770 km2 by the 2030s) is sharp but smaller than the grid's cell.

sources.note: Opened by reviewer se-04-b: ICJ judgment of 23 May 2008 (Pedra Branca to Singapore, Middle Rocks to Malaysia); Horsburgh Lighthouse 1850-1851; Malaysian map of 21 December 1979.

notes: The state begins on 9 August 1965, two years before Cliopatria's first Singapore shape (1967): a new 1965 keyframe extends the shape back, and the Malaysia dossier's 1965 keyframe drops Singapore at the same date. Page budget (1-2) was spent on the Singapore and Singapore in Malaysia articles. The Pedra Branca ruling (2008) is a conf-1 event from the researcher's memory because the Singapore page gives no date; it is off the land grid. Land reclamation is not a dated event on the page (it gives only 'roughly 580 km2 in the 1960s to 770 km2 by the 2030s'). Britain 'pulled its military out of Singapore' in October 1971 (page): the bases are not an occupation of Singapore's land in any source opened. 'Border issues exist with Malaysia and Indonesia' (page) with no detail. The boundary with Johor is not described beyond 'the Straits of Johor along with the State of Johor in Malaysia to the north' and the Johor-Singapore Causeway. The seed lists malaysia and republic-of-indonesia as neighbours from 1967 (within 25 km). Reviewer se-04-b (2026-10-20): the 2008 gain of Pedra Branca from Malaysia was removed from the ledger: no land changed hands. Singapore (and the United Kingdom before it, which built Horsburgh Lighthouse there in 1850-1851) administered the rock throughout; Malaysia first claimed it on a map of 21 December 1979, and the International Court of Justice found on 23 May 2008 that 'sovereignty over Pedra Branca belongs to Singapore' (Middle Rocks to Malaysia). Page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedra_Branca_dispute.
